title: redundant visual signals
name: Redundant visual signals
rule: Separate the consequential option with space and redundant visual signals (color, icon, size, alignment), not the label alone.

citation.source: NN/g — Dangerous UX: Consequential Options Close to Benign Options

pass_when: The consequential option is separated with space and more than one of color, icon, size, alignment — not the label alone.
fail_when: Distinction is label-only, or a single non-label cue with no space.
overview: Consequential options are separated by space plus redundant visual signals.
apply_when: Distinguishing a dangerous option near safer peers in the same view.
not_when: Ordinary peer actions that share equal risk and need no danger separation.
agent_hint: Separate consequential options with space and multiple cues, not label alone.
description: A consequential option should be separated with space and redundant visual signals—color, icon, size, alignment—not the label alone. Label-only distinction, or a single cue without space, is easy to miss under speed or stress. Stack multiple cues when danger sits near benign choices so the separation survives a quick glance. Equal-risk peer actions that share the same stakes do not need this danger treatment.
